Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working diagnosis and rationale: Acute gastroenteritis (tummy bug), most likely viral etiology given acute onset after takeout exposure; symptoms include watery diarrhea, abdominal cramping, feverish sensation, and transient vomiting with no reported blood in stool.
- Relevant differential diagnoses and reasoning (aligned with transcript and DDx):
  - Viral gastroenteritis — High
  - Bacterial gastroenteritis/food poisoning (e.g., Salmonella, Campylobacter) — Medium
  - Post-infectious lactose intolerance / IBD flare — Low to Medium
- Differential diagnoses (summary): See above
- Plan and management priorities:
  - Hydration and symptomatic care (oral rehydration with Dioralyte or similar)
  - Paracetamol for fever/weakness: route not documented; dose/route/frequency: two tablets up to four times daily
  - Rest and take time off work for 2–3 days
  - Avoid antibiotics at this time
  - If symptoms persist or worsen, follow-up in 3–4 days and consider stool testing
  - Consider stool sample testing if symptoms persist to evaluate for bacterial or other etiologies

Management Plan

- Hydration: Emphasize oral rehydration (Dioralyte or equivalent) to replenish fluids and electrolytes
- Medications: Paracetamol for fever/weakness as described above; no antibiotics indicated at this stage
- Activity/work: Take 2–3 days off work to allow recovery
- Follow-up and monitoring: Reassess in 3–4 days if no improvement; stool testing considered if persistent
- Education: Stay hydrated; seek care for signs of dehydration or worsening symptoms; return sooner if severe symptoms or red flags develop

Consider

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits): Not recorded
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral: Not recorded
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support): Not recorded
- CTG registration: Not recorded
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test): Not recorded

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Viral gastroenteritis
  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Acute onset diarrhea (watery), initial vomiting, feverish sensation, no blood in stool; recent takeout exposure supports a common gastroenteritis etiologic pattern.
- Bacterial gastroenteritis/food poisoning
  - Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Takeout meal 4 days before symptoms; diarrhea without blood; cramps; incubation compatible with some foodborne pathogens.
- Post-infectious lactose intolerance / IBD flare
  - Likelihood: Low to Medium
  - Justification: Left-lower-quadrant cramps with diarrhea after GI illness; no prior IBD history; possible post-infectious change or intolerance, though less likely given the acute presentation.

- Giardia or other parasitic enteritis
  - Likelihood: Low
  - Justification: Diarrhea and cramps; less likely given the rapid onset after a food exposure

  - History is detailed for GI symptoms and exposures; physical examination and vitals were not recorded in the transcript, limiting objective assessment. Overall, the history supports an acute gastroenteritis assessment.
